changelog.reason: Initial freeze for the HN aidevforum evidence run
Option 1: per-item coin flip, p_learned=0.5, salt hn-aidevforum-2026-11-17.2. Arm and choice_prob live in assignments.jsonl only.

Slot-level coin flip. A run draws one arm per posting slot from the same remaining pool. Arms are L (ranker) and B (baseline). Analysis is intention-to-treat on slots. Sample hash salt stays hn-aidevforum-2026-11-17.2.

Primary lift claim stays intention-to-treat on all posted slots. n_contrast (L != B) and the contrast-subset effect are explanatory only. ITT difference is about contrast_rate times the contrast-subset effect. Salt unchanged.

hn-aidevforum.question: Does the learned ranking pick better aidevforum topics than the frozen baseline?

randomization.analysis: intention-to-treat two-proportion test on all posted slots; p=0.5 so weights are equal; no peeking except safety stop
randomization.explanatory: n_contrast and effect within L != B decisions; not a substitute for the ITT claim
randomization.dilution: itt_effect ≈ contrast_rate × contrast_subset_effect; with contrast_rate 0.48 a 10pp ITT lift needs about 21pp in the contrast subset

ranker.prior: rag_score descending until 200 auto-labeled posts and rater/auto agreement >= 0.9
ranker.model: L2 logistic regression on allowlisted features
ranker.fallback: ranker exception logs arm B with fallback=true

notes: Blind labels judge relevance for AI development.
A relevance rejection or duplicate is a quality failure.
Rater must not see arm, policy, rank, or auto scores.
Enqueue successful and failed HTTP attempts.
Daily audit compares job attempts with enqueued items.
A posted item without a prior decision record is an audit alarm.
Both arms choose from the same RAG-filtered, de-duplicated pool.
Primary claim is ITT on all posted slots. n_contrast explains where any ITT difference comes from.
Sim n_contrast and sim contrast-subset effects are mechanics, not quality evidence.

podcast-buzzsprout.question: Reliability and cost of a daily publish, not a lift test.
